title: Tenant-scoped correlation IDs + targeted tracing + emergency graceful-degrade for opaque 5xx waves
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Background: Over the last 36 hours we have received three separate escalations from high-value tenants reporting opaque 5xx bursts and elevated tail latency when the hosted API experiences tenant surges. Current mitigation (rate limits + conservative backoffs) reduced surface but did not prevent cascading retries and client-side amplification. Root signals point to a combination of (A) missing request-level correlation between front proxy and backend workers, (B) high sampling thresholds on traces making triage slow, and (C) a rare kernel-scheduler path in the serving runtime that stalls when a tenant's KV-cache becomes contended under high concurrency.

Scope: This ticket contains a multi-pronged emergency fix: 1) propagate a tenant-scoped correlation_id end-to-end (proxy -> api-gateway -> runtime) so individual request trees are visible in traces and logs, 2) enable targeted high-fidelity tracing for affected tenants (short window, dynamic sampling), and 3) deploy a graceful-degrade toggle that forces lightweight model-variant fallback for tenants under suspected kernel-scheduler stalls while we patch the runtime.

Goals: Reduce time-to-root-cause for customer escalations (from hours to minutes), prevent tenant-triggered retry storms by enabling per-tenant fallback routing, and ship a short-term runtime patch + longer-term kernel fix.

Proposed solution:
- Correlation IDs: Add X-Redwood-CID header at gateway; ensure propagation into runtime logs (structured log key correlation_id) and attach to all spans. Update SDKs to unambiguously return correlation_id to customers when present.
- Tracing: Introduce a tenant-targeted sampling API (admin endpoint) so SRE/SEs can flip high-sampling for a tenant for a 15-30 min window. Ensure traces include batch and kernel-scheduling span boundaries.
- Graceful-degrade: Implement a feature-flagged routing rule that will, for a given tenant, route new requests to a lower-memory model variant (reduced KV cache pressure) with explicit response header (X-Redwood-Degraded: true) and a client-visible retry-after hint when applicable.
- Runtime patch: Hotfix commit to guard the rare scheduler path by adding a 3ms cooperative yield and improved contention metrics. Will be rolled to a canary subset of nodes first.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge correlation-id instrumentation PR and deploy to gateway + api-gateway services.
2) Turn on tenant-scoped high-fidelity sampling for affected tenants (SRE-run).
3) Release and canary the runtime hotfix to 5% capacity for a single region; monitor KV contention, 5xx rate, and latency per-tenant.
4) If canary is clean for 60m, expand to 25% then 100% per region.
5) If regression seen, flip graceful-degrade for affected tenants and rollback hotfix to previous runtime build while we escalate.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for header propagation and SDK surface changes.
- Integration test harness that replays tenant burst load with KV-cache contention to validate graceful-degrade behavior.
- Observability: add per-tenant 1m metrics for active connections, KV-cache locks, and scheduler-yield counts. Dashboards: link below.

Customer comms: Draft email & support playbook prepared (Confluence link). Notify impacted customers with correlation_id and suggested temporary client-side retry configuration.

Artifacts & links:
- Runbook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/tenant-5xx-escalation-playbook
- Alert dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted/tenant-5xx-waves
- Patch PR (runtime): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428
- Correlation PR (gateway): https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/987

Success criteria: Per-tenant 5xx rate reduced by >=80% within 30 minutes of targeted intervention OR ability to keep affected tenant traffic at degraded variant with <2x latency increase and no customer-visible errors for the duration of surge.

Postmortem actions: Formal blameless postmortem in 72 hours, add unit+integration test to prevent scheduler regressions, and create long-term plan to remove graceful-degrade after runtime fix is hardened.
